note: A NUMBER IN A DOC COMMENT IS A NUMBER THAT WILL BE WRONG. The Rill Task 3, measured across three fix rounds. Round 2 rewrote a stale attribution block two ways at once: it turned four figures into Rust locals the test computes and prints, and it left two more as hand-typed literals. NONE of the four printed ones drifted. BOTH hand-typed ones were wrong on arrival, in that same commit, into the very defect the commit existed to fix - each transcribed from an ADJACENT population rather than the one under discussion. One said 96 crossings, which is the floor constant belonging to a neighbouring test that injects 25 extremes; the owning test computes 88. The other said an expectation of 0.67 loud vertices, which is 395 x 25/14606 - the injected extremes substituted for the 91 loud vertices - where the right figure is 395 x 91/14606 = 2.46. The second one refuted itself two sentences later, which is the only reason it was catchable by reading. Rule: if the test that owns the population can compute the number, make it a local and print it; if it cannot, name the population beside the figure so a reader can tell which one it came from. Second technique, and it cost a whole round: THE WORKSPACE TWO-TEST GUARD REJECTS THE ENTIRE BASH COMMAND, INCLUDING ANY EDIT CHAINED AHEAD OF IT. A python heredoc that rewrote a doc comment was chained with two test invocations, the guard refused the command before anything ran, I re-ran only the test half under the override, saw green, and reported the edit as landed. git diff --stat for that file across the commit is empty. The green was logically incapable of witnessing the change because no test reads a doc comment. After any edit to a file no test can observe, the verification is git diff, not a test run.
